newsitem.title: USA: Retired US general sounds alarm on nuclear arms.
newsitem.headline: Retired US general sounds alarm on nuclear arms.

text.p: Retired Air Force Gen. George Lee Butler, once commander in chief of the U.S. nuclear arsenal, now says U.S. nuclear policy is "fundamentally irrational," on grounds that such arms threaten humanity.
Butler is due to make a speech in Washington Wednesday advocating the urgent elimination of nuclear weapons around the globe, the Washington Post reported in Wednesday editions.
Butler told the newspaper that eliminating nuclear weapons is the only way to forestall a horrible nuclear accident and prevent warheads from falling into the hands of rogue states or extremists.
He will be joined in making this plea for disarmament by Andrew Goodpaster, a former supreme allied commander in Europe.

Goodpaster also helped organised a statement by 60 generals and admirals around the world calling for additional nuclear arms cuts and the phased elimination of nuclear arms, to be released on Thursday.

Signers include Gen. John Gavin, another former supreme allied commander in Europe, and Gen. Charles Horner, former commander of the U.S. Space Command and a key officer in the 1991 Gulf War, the Post reported.
"Nuclear weapons are inherently dangerous, hugely expensive, militarily inefficient and morally indefensible," Butler told the Post.
